products.policy: Do not equate absence of alternative splice declarations with absence of proteolytic maturation. Evaluate source/construct and product-policy representation during review; no new product assertion yet.

phylogenetic_reading.reading: Human GDF2 is the sequence-exact 429-residue AN350/PTN002483793 terminal. Cytokine and extracellular-region IBDs are at AN0; endothelial-proliferation and BMP-signaling IBDs are at AN340/Euteleostomi. All donor identities map to descendants of their actual assertion, and incoming, full retained IBD and main-slice donor sets match. Human self-evidence in all four is legitimate, including the single self-donor BMP-signaling assertion; no circularity or low-donor-count objection is inferred. These are ancestry facts, not final decisions on every biological scope.

review_delta.before: Authentic abstract checked. ALK1 solution structure and binding experiments support BMP9 recognition; the proposed complex model is not treated as a new ternary crystal structure.
review_delta.after: Selected full Methods/Results support direct human BMP9 binding to bacterially produced human ALK1 ectodomain by SPR. Separate NIH-3T3 antagonist assays measure phospho-SMAD. The NMR structure is unbound receptor; ligand-complex geometry is modeled, not an experimentally solved complex.

review_delta.before: Authentic abstract checked. Receptor-active covalent and noncovalent BMP9 dimers differ in signaling persistence/stability; these are biochemical states, not splice products.
review_delta.after: Selected full Methods/Results distinguish covalently linked and noncovalent BMP9 solution dimers, both receptor-active, with different signaling persistence and proteolytic susceptibility. These are redox states, not natural splice products. Serum experiments used spiked recombinant ligand; endogenous clearance was not directly measured. Structure 4MPL contains ligand without ALK1.
